name: Repository
description: Several agent runs on one small library, read as a code forge shows them: any run or runs chosen, pull requests with their commits, diffs and reviews, issues, discussions and agents, each run's measures side by side, so the runs' setups can be compared issue by issue and a pull request's whole story is one click away.
data: One folder per run, runs/<run>/, matched by runs/*.json, runs/*.jsonl and runs/*.csv: manifest.json (the run's agents, the approvals a merge needs and its brief), events.jsonl (the forge's events: issues, pull requests, pushes with their diffs, reviews, comments, merges, closes and reopens), board.jsonl (the discussion) and agents/<name>.jsonl (each agent's transcript, whose last message is its sign-off note). r3's forge data is an export instead: export/issues.csv, pulls.csv (a row per pull request, with its merge or close), commits.csv (each commit's patch in a cell over several lines), comments.csv and reviews.json. Every run works the same backlog, so issue numbers and titles match across runs. The reader cleans: manifest keys that differ by run; r4's events in a later schema with renamed fields, a push's diff among them; times in ISO 8601 with or without an offset, epoch milliseconds, and local time in the manifest's timezone; redelivered events (a repeated id); events logged out of order; a cut-off last line, reported with any other line that does not parse; a table cell over several lines; an agent the manifest lists with no transcript; numbers written as free text; a pull request with no area label; a review with no reviewer; a post with no time; a force-push; and a reopened pull request. The reader's opening comment names every field.
